map.失速速度由最大升力系数决定。: Stall speed is determined by the maximum lift coefficient.
map.重量越大失速越快。: The greater the weight, the higher the stall speed.
map.增升装置提高 C_Lmax 降低 V_s。: High-lift devices raise C_Lmax and lower V_s.
map.由重量 W、密度 ρ、面积 S 与最大升力系数 C_Lmax 算失速速度 Vs=: Compute the stall speed Vs=√(2W/(ρS·C_Lmax)) from the weight W, density ρ, area S and maximum lift coefficient C_Lmax.
map.评估起飞/着陆安全速度裕度（通常取 1.2–1.3 Vs）。: Assess the takeoff/landing safety speed margin (usually 1.2-1.3 Vs).
map.对比不同重量/高度（密度）下的失速速度变化。: Compare the stall-speed change at different weights/altitudes (densities).
map.重量 W=60000 N、密度 ρ=1.225、面积 S=20 m²、C_Lma: Weight W=60000 N, density ρ=1.225, area S=20 m² and C_Lmax=1.5. Vs=√(2×60000/(1.225×20×1.5))=√(120000/36.75)=√3265≈57.1 m/s. The approach reference speed is about 1.3×Vs≈74 m/s.
map.为什么重了失速速度更高？: Why is the stall speed higher when heavier?
map.要保持 L=W，重量大需更大速度（或更大 C_L）。故满载比空载更易在低速失速，: To keep L=W, a greater weight needs a higher speed (or a larger C_L). So a fully loaded aircraft stalls more easily at low speed, and takeoff/landing must compute Vs at the maximum landing weight and leave a margin.
map.高度影响失速速度吗？: Does altitude affect the stall speed?
map.影响。高空密度低，同重量下需更高真速才能产生同等升力，故失速真速随高度上升；但指: It does. At high altitude the density is low, so at the same weight a higher true speed is needed to produce the same lift, so the stall true speed rises with altitude; but the stall indicated airspeed (IAS) is essentially unchanged, because IAS is proportional to dynamic pressure.
map.失速速度（本页代码口径）：V_s=√(2W÷(ρ×S×C_Lmax))（m/s，: Stall speed (page code convention): V_s=√(2W÷(ρ×S×C_Lmax)) (m/s; W weight in N, ρ air density kg/m³, S wing area m², C_Lmax maximum lift coefficient); linked values: km/h=V_s×3.6, plus a stall-speed lookup table generated by scanning weight multiples. Validation: the four fields are required by input guards and must be valid numbers, otherwise a prompt is shown and the calculation stops. Criteria: no fixed grading; V_s is proportional to the square root of weight and inversely proportional to the square root of density, so takeoff/landing stall speed increases at high altitude (low density).
